subject: Fraud Watch: how vendor impersonation emails look in 2026
text:
FRAUD WATCH | November 2026

Business email compromise losses passed $3.1 billion last year, and vendor impersonation remains the most common play. A typical message reads:

   "Please be informed that we have changed our bank account. Kindly update
    your records and remit all future payments to routing 026009593, account
    4471002983. The old account is no longer in use."

What to look for
- A reply-to address that differs from the sender
- Urgency ("before today's run")
- A new account at a different bank than the vendor has used for years
- Pressure to skip callback verification

What to do
- Call the vendor at a number from your own records, never from the email
- Require a signed letter and a second approver for any bank change
- Enrol in Positive Pay and ACH debit blocks through Treasury Online
